result: h07. **Where the URL comes from (why the browser requests it):** the API never returns raw avatar bytes — `convertUserFromStore` rewrites a base64 avatar into the path `/file/users/{username}/avatar`, and `` puts that in an ``. - `convertUserFromStore` — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:16` (URL built at :36) - `UserAvatar` — `web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:9` (``) **Serving path — hop per line:** - `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` (route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121` (wired at `server/server.go:81-82`) - `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168` - `FileServerService.getCurrentUser` → `auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708`, `server/auth/authenticator.go:190` *(only when `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is false; gate at fileserver.go:173-181)* - `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715` - `Store.GetUser` (cache hit only when `find.ID` is set — here it's `Username`, so it always falls through) — `store/user.go:148` - `Store.ListUsers` (+ `userCache.Set`) — `store/user.go:136` - `Driver.ListUsers` (interface) — `store/driver.go:47`; concrete driver chosen in `store/db/db.go:14` - `DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (also `store/db/mysql/user.go:84`, `store/db/postgres/user.go:87`) - `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?` via `db.QueryContext` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:151-172` **Back out:** `FileServerService.parseDataURI` (`fileserver.go:737`) splits the stored `data:;base64,...` string, the MIME type is checked against `avatarAllowedTypes` (`fileserver.go:74`), security + cache headers are set (`setSecurityHeaders`, `fileserver.go:764`), and the decoded bytes go out via `c.Blob` (`fileserver.go:206`). The key fact about the data layer: avatars are **not** attachments/blob storage. They live inline in the `user.avatar_url` column as a base64 data URI, so the terminal hop is the user-row query, not `store.GetAttachment` or S3/local-file access.
